note: The attacker-controlled FONT string from the mapfile is heap-allocated into label->font of the legend's embedded labelObj; this heap pointer is the object that later gets freed twice.

code: freeLabel(label);       /* free any structures allocated before EOF */
note: When the input ends (EOF) inside the LABEL block, loadLabel's error path frees the label contents (including label->font) even though the legend object still owns this embedded label; the refcount drops to 0 but the label is not reset, so the later cleanup path will free it again.
loadLabel reports failure to its caller after already freeing the label contents, so the caller aborts the map parse and eventually enters msLoadMap's error cleanup.
loadLegend propagates the parse failure up to loadMapInternal; the legend label whose contents were already freed stays inside the map object for later cleanup.
The failed LABEL parse makes loadMapInternal return MS_FAILURE, which drives msLoadMap into its error path that calls msFreeMap(map).
msLoadMap's error cleanup frees the partially parsed map object, which in turn calls freeLegend() on the legend whose label contents were already freed by loadLabel.
Second invocation of freeLabel on the same legend label during map cleanup; the label refcount is already 0, so the refcount guard does not prevent the re-free.
msFree(label->font) executes a second time on the same heap pointer that was already freed in loadLabel's EOF error path, producing the double free.
